# Coder task 010 — find the change that makes the board hang

**Opened 2026-09-24.** Thinker → board agent. Do not edit this file; write everything in `REPORT.md`.

**This is a BOARD MEASUREMENT task, not an RTL task. You must not change any `.scala` file.**
If you think you have found the bug in the RTL, write it in the REPORT and stop. Someone else fixes it.

| # | Rule |

## 1. The problem, in one paragraph

On 2026-09-24 the VCU118 board ran the same omnetpp workload twice in one boot. The first run finished
normally in **17.2 minutes**. The second produced no output for **86 minutes** and the Linux console
stopped responding to Enter — the board was wedged, and only reprogramming the FPGA recovered it. The
question is which RTL change introduced that. The suspicion that the counter-zeroing option `--zero`
caused it has been **ruled out** (see §2), so do not spend time on it.

## 2. What is already known — do not re-derive any of this

| # | Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | **`sbc_read --zero` cannot stall anything.** It writes `SBC_StatsReset` (0x3B8), which in the generated Verilog reaches exactly one module (`PerfCounters.io_clearStats`) and drives only read-only counter registers. It has no path to any ready/valid, victim mux or MSHR state | netlist trace; and 4 board runs with `--zero` completed normally, two of them with migration confirmed active |
| K2 | The board currently runs `FPGADualRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBCPLRU-2026-09-18.bit` — **DUAL Rocket**, 64 KB 16-way L2, 50 MHz. Its Vivado session ran Sep 18 09:24–09:49, i.e. the uncommitted tree that became **`201ebae` (SBC 008 c2)** | `scripts/ssbc_scripts/vivado.log`; the bitstream's own `.vivado.log` |
| K3 | That bitstream is 008 c2, **not** 009: `attempted − migrations` equals `dstAbortDirty+Held+Both` exactly in every dump (209,997 and 215,651 in two runs). That identity only holds with 008-c2 abort semantics | two independent board dumps |
| K4 | **Reference timing: 1033 s (17.2 min)** for one completed workload, twice, agreeing to 0.16%. `L2_Cycles ÷ 50e6` equals the board's own `date +%s` measurement exactly | runs at 00:51 and 07:48 on 2026-09-24 |
| K5 | **The workload prints NOTHING between start and finish.** `--cmdenv-status-frequency` does not work on this board: omnetpp's wall clock reads `Elapsed: 0.000s` even at 100%, so Cmdenv never emits progress. **Silence is therefore not evidence of a hang** — a healthy 17-minute run is equally silent. You must use the heartbeat loop in §4 | SPEC `omnetpp.ini` sets `cmdenv-status-frequency = 5000000s`; a run with the override still printed only the start and end banners |
| K6 | The hang signature: the run reaches `** Event #1 ... 0% completed` and never reaches `100% completed`. It dies **during** the simulation, not in teardown | the 01:16 run |
| K7 | The one condition the hang had that the two successful runs did not: it was the **second** workload run of its boot, after ~5.5 M migrations had already accumulated | run order in the 00:51 log |
| K7b | **REPRODUCED 2026-09-24 08:10, and it is fast.** On the same bitstream, run 1 of the boot completed (`ITER_RC=0 ITER_SECS=1033`); run 2, started immediately after with no reboot, wedged **between t=1s and t=61s**. At t=1s it was healthy: `accessA=914,539` in 0.657 s (1.39 M/s), `migrations=14,729`, `parked=15`. So a trial costs boot + ~17 min (R1) + ~1 min (R2), not hours | heartbeat log `uart_20260924_074558.log` |
| K7c | **The wedge is hard.** The heartbeat is a *shell* loop, independent of the workload, and it stopped — so the shell stopped executing, not just the benchmark. A console probe after the wedge received **0 bytes** from the board across Enter x2 and Ctrl-C, on two separate picocom sessions. No character echo at all means the kernel tty path cannot run, i.e. the core cannot complete a cacheable access. Only reprogramming the FPGA recovers it | probe logs, 2026-09-24 08:25 and 08:28 |
| K8 | `SBC_MigrateEnable` **resets to 0**. A run without an explicit `--migrate=on` measures a plain L2 and proves nothing. This has already produced two wasted sessions | 2026-09-24 sessions |

## 3. The plan — find the newest bitstream on which omnetpp still completes

Walk the single-core 64 KB bitstreams in build order and run each through the two-boot recipe in §4.
The answer is the newest one that passes both boots. **Core count is not being studied in this task** —
run single-core images only and ignore the Dual image except as the known-bad reference.

### ⚠️ File dates and file names are both unreliable

- **`ls -lt` shows the COPY time, not the build time.** The Dual image is stamped Sep 21 but its own
  `.vivado.log` says it was built Sep 18. Only two bitstreams still have a build log, so the order below
  comes from the date in the **filename** — treat it as approximate.
- **Two pairs of files are byte-identical under different names** (sha256, 2026-09-24):
  `...SBCPLRU-008-c2B-7494296-wip-2026-09-17.bit` **=** `...SBCPLRU-009-c1-2026-09-19.bit`, and
  `...256K...old-rules-pre007-2026-09-15.bit` **=** `...256K...random-source-evict-2026-09-17.bit`.
  So `009-c1-2026-09-19.bit` is **not** a 009 build.
- **`sha256sum` every bitstream before you run it and record the hash in the REPORT, not the file name.**

### The candidates, oldest build first

All are single-core, 64 KB, 16-way, 50 MHz. Path prefix: `chipyard/fpga/bitstream_storage/`.

| # | sha256 | file | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `abb2e3150b77` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBC-c0c1c2-breakeven-2026-09-16.bit` | 007 c0–c2 era. **No PLRU register** (`ConfigSBC`, not `ConfigSBCPLRU`) — `0x490` reads 0, which is random, so `--policy=random` still succeeds |
| 2 | `1fa244ec92e7` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBC-preferEvictable-experiment-2026-09-16.bit` | an **experiment** build — parameters may not be the defaults. Use only if #1 and #3 do not settle it, and say so |
| **3** | `e41f780c67ff` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBCPLRU-008-c2B-7494296-wip-2026-09-17.bit` | **START HERE.** 008 c2 option-B WIP on `7494296` |
| 4 | `3bea9add4cb8` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBCPLRU-009-c1-rebuilt-2026-09-19.bit` | build confirmed Sep 19 00:49. Uncommitted "009 c1" WIP — no matching commit exists |
| 5 | `afa13ca9b010` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBCPLRU-009-c2-739bd2a-2026-09-21.bit` | `739bd2a` |
| 6 | `7b83bcbc8f02` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBCPLRU-739bd2a-unverified-tree-2026-09-22.bit` | `739bd2a` |
| 7 | `7fb33ce6357c` | `FPGASingleRocketVCU118L18K64K16WL2ConfigSBCPLRU-009-c2-739bd2a-clean-rebuild-2026-09-22.bit` | `739bd2a`, clean rebuild |

⚠️ **5, 6 and 7 are three DIFFERENT bitstreams built from the same commit** (`739bd2a`) — different
place-and-route runs. If some of them pass and others fail, the fault is **timing / place-and-route, not
RTL**. That is a real possibility here: a known open bug (B7-2) is a Vivado DRC combinational-loop
failure on a 256 KB build of this design. Say so explicitly if you see it; do not average them.

### The search

Start at **#3**. Then:

- **#3 PASSES** → walk **newer** (#4, #5, …) until one fails. The last pass is the answer.
- **#3 FAILS** → walk **older** (#2, #1) until one passes. The first pass is the answer.

At most four trials either way. Stop as soon as you have one pass and one fail that are adjacent in the
list, and name both.

## 4. The recipe — two boots per bitstream

Everything in one `tmux` session per bitstream. Policy is `random` for every run; do not vary it.
Every run uses `--zero`. `ITER_RC` must be `0` on every run.

```
BOOT A   program the FPGA
         R1  omnetpp, migrate OFF, --zero          <- timing baseline; parks nothing
         R2  omnetpp, migrate ON,  --zero          <- SAME boot, no reboot
BOOT B   reprogram the FPGA
         R3  omnetpp, migrate ON,  --zero          <- the FIRST and only run of this boot
```

R1 must come before R2 in boot A: the migrate-OFF run parks nothing, and that is the only thing that
makes `--reset-all` legal before R2.

If R2 wedges, boot A is over — the console is dead and only reprogramming recovers it. Capture §6, then
reprogram and do boot B anyway; R3 still tells you something (see the table below).

### Verdict for one bitstream

| R2 (ON, 2nd run of boot A) | R3 (ON, 1st run of boot B) | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| completes | completes | **PASS** — this bitstream runs omnetpp |
| wedges | completes | **FAIL.** Migration alone is not enough; the trigger needs a prior run in the same boot, i.e. accumulated SBC state |
| wedges | wedges | **FAIL.** Migration ON alone is enough — the "second run" framing is wrong and should be dropped |
| completes | wedges | **FAIL**, and surprising. Re-run both boots before reporting it |

### 4.1 Program and boot, and get R1

```bash
cd /home/damith/Research/repos/chipyard_performance_eval/chipyard/scripts/ssbc_scripts
sha256sum <bitstream path>          # record this in the REPORT, not the file name
./tmp.exp -hangtest migoff -bit <bitstream path> -iters 1
```

That programs the FPGA, boots Linux, verifies `sbc_read` on the board, mounts the SD card, stages the
benchmark, sets `--migrate=off`, runs R1 and exits picocom leaving the board booted.

⚠️ **Use the script only for program + boot + R1. Drive R2 and R3 by hand (§4.2, §4.3).** The script's
own hang detector is a plain 1800 s timeout, which works only because a healthy run is 1033 s — it
cannot tell a wedge from a slow run, because the workload prints nothing either way (K5). The manual
heartbeat can, and that distinction is the whole point of this task.

Reconnect with:

```bash
./connect_serial.sh        # or: picocom -b 115200 --logfile ../logs/uart_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log /dev/ttyUSB2
```

### 4.2 Set the switch and CONFIRM it (before R2 and before R3)

```sh
/root/sbc_read --policy=random          # every run in this task is random; do not vary it
/root/sbc_read --reset-all --migrate=on # legal ONLY when nothing is parked
/root/sbc_read | head -1                # the line MUST contain  migrate: ON
```

- If `--reset-all` is refused ("N line(s) still parked"), **do not pass `--force`.** Use plain
  `--migrate=on` and note in the REPORT that this run did not start cold.
- If the `migrate` line says OFF, **stop**. The run would measure a plain L2 and prove nothing (K8).
  This has already wasted two sessions.

### 4.3 One timed run, with the heartbeat

This is the instrument. Run it for R2 and for R3.

```sh
cd /root/test_dir/520.omnetpp_r_run_ref
/root/sbc_read --zero > /dev/null
HS=$(date +%s)
./omnetpp_r_base.riscv-64 -c General -r 0 --sim-time-limit=0.002s > wl.out 2> wl.err &
W=$!
while kill -0 $W 2>/dev/null; do
  echo "HB t=$(( $(date +%s) - HS ))s"
  /root/sbc_read | head -1
  sleep 60
done
wait $W; echo "ITER_RC=$? ITER_SECS=$(( $(date +%s) - HS ))"
```

`ITER_RC` must be `0`. **An rc of 127 means the binary was not found and the run measured nothing** —
that has already happened once and produced a normal-looking counter dump, so always check it.

For R1 (migrate OFF) the same loop works; or use `tmp.exp -hangtest migoff` as in §4.1.

## 5. How to tell a hang from a slow run

Watch `accessA` in the heartbeat line. It counts inner-A requests and normally advances by roughly one
million per second.

| observation | conclusion |
|---|---|
| **the heartbeat line itself stops appearing** | **HUNG, hard.** The loop is a shell loop independent of the workload, so its silence means the shell stopped executing. This is the confirmed signature (K7c). Go to §6 immediately. Expect it within 60 s of R2 starting |
| `accessA` unchanged across **3 consecutive heartbeats** (3 minutes) | **HUNG.** Go to §6 immediately |
| elapsed passes **3100 s** (3× the 1033 s reference) with `accessA` still advancing | very slow, not hung. Let it run and record the final time |
| `sbc_read` itself stops printing | the shell cannot run, so the core cannot complete a cacheable access. **HUNG at the fabric level.** Go to §6 |
| `L2_Cycles` still advancing | **proves nothing.** It is free-running off the L2 clock and keeps counting even when the core is wedged. Do not quote it as proof of life |

## 6. When it hangs — capture this BEFORE rebooting

This is the only chance to see the wedge from the inside. Do not reprogram until you have:

1. The last 5 heartbeat lines (they carry `accessA`, `migrations`, `parked`, `secondSearch`, `L2_Cycles`).
2. Three more `/root/sbc_read | head -1` reads, 30 s apart, if it still answers. Record which counters
   are frozen and which still move.
3. Press **Ctrl-C** once. Record whether a `#` prompt comes back:
   - **prompt returns** → the shell is alive, so the L2 still serves the console; only the workload was stuck.
   - **nothing returns** → the core cannot complete a cacheable access: an L2/fabric wedge.
4. Press Enter twice more and record whether anything echoes.
5. The full UART log path.

## 7. What to record for every run

| field | where it comes from |
|---|---|
| bitstream file name | you chose it |
| cores (Single/Dual) | the file name |
| run label | R1 (OFF) / R2 (ON, 2nd of boot A) / R3 (ON, 1st of boot B) |
| migrate | the confirmed `migrate :` line, not what you asked for |
| policy | the `policy :` line |
| `ITER_RC` | must be 0 |
| `ITER_SECS` | wall seconds |
| `L2_Cycles` | from the final dump; `÷ 50e6` must agree with `ITER_SECS` |
| `accessA`, `primaryHit`, `secondaryHit`, `dataMiss` | final dump |
| `memReads`, `memWrites` | final dump — **report these two separately, never only their sum** |
| `migrations`, `attempted`, `aborted`, `parked` | final dump |
| `secondSearch`, `secondaryMiss` | final dump |
| outcome | completed / hung / rc≠0 |

Sanity checks that must hold on every completed run; report any that fail:

- `accessA = primaryHit + secondaryHit + dataMiss + upgradeMiss` (±38)
- `dataMiss + upgradeMiss = memReads + memAcqPerm`
- `L2_Cycles ÷ 50e6 ≈ ITER_SECS`
